headline: The Social Life, Invitations & Dating Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach and explain games, plans and customs, rescue a plan that falls apart, refuse an unsafe request, report an incident to police or emergency services, and agree honest terms for staying in touch, all in Spanish.

lessons.title: Teach Your Hostel Friends a Card Game from Home
lessons.objective: Explain the steps and the logic of a card game, then check understanding as friends explain it back.

words.note: The opposite is boca arriba (face up).
Common in Chile; la puntuación is also understood.
For a woman: la ganadora.

words.en: First, 7 cards are dealt to each person.
words.es: Primero se reparten 7 cartas a cada uno.

words.en: Then each person draws a card from the deck.
words.es: Luego cada uno saca una carta del mazo.

words.en: The joker replaces any card; that's why it's worth so much.
words.es: El comodín reemplaza cualquier carta; por eso vale tanto.

words.en: Nobody shows their cards because that way there's no cheating.
words.es: Nadie muestra sus cartas porque así no hay trampa.

words.en: Can you explain it to me in your own words?
words.es: ¿Me lo explicas con tus propias palabras?
words.note: Informal tú, fine between hostel friends.

words.en: Almost, but the points are counted at the end of each round.
words.es: Casi, pero los puntos se cuentan al final de cada ronda.

words.en: Do you get how the points are counted?
words.note: ¿Cachai? is Chilean slang for 'you get it?'; informal, only with friends.
Bacán is Chilean slang for great or cool; informal.

lessons.speaking: You are teaching the AI, playing your hostel friends Camila and Tomás, a card game from home: explain the steps in order and the reason behind each rule with primero, luego, porque and por eso, then have them explain it back to you.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso: primero se reparten las cartas, por eso nadie las ve)

examples.es: Primero se reparten las cartas boca abajo, por eso nadie las ve.
examples.en: First the cards are dealt face down, so nobody sees them.

examples.es: Luego se suman los puntos, porque el ganador se decide al final.
examples.en: Then the points are added up, because the winner is decided at the end.

lessons.title: Explain How the Language Exchange Works to a Newcomer
lessons.objective: Explain the format and unwritten rules of a language exchange and correct a newcomer's wrong idea about it.

words.note: The Spanish of Buenos Aires and Montevideo, with vos and the 'sh' sound in ll and y.

words.en: the hookup (flirting to pick someone up)
words.note: Argentine slang; informal.
For a man: el organizador.
For a woman: la recién llegada.

words.en: Here you speak Spanish for half an hour and English for half an hour.
words.es: Acá se habla media hora en español y media en inglés.
words.note: Acá is the usual word for 'here' in Argentina.

words.en: If someone doesn't understand, you just ask, no shame.
words.es: Si alguien no entiende, se pregunta sin vergüenza.

words.en: When the bell rings, you switch tables.
words.es: Si suena la campana, se cambia de mesa.

words.en: No, it's not a speed-dating night.
words.es: No, no es una noche de citas rápidas.

words.en: People come to practice, not to look for a hookup.
words.es: La gente viene a practicar, no a buscar levante.
words.note: Informal; levante is Argentine slang.

words.en: If they correct you, it's nothing personal.
words.es: Si te corrigen, no es nada personal.

words.en: Flor, will you correct me if I explain something wrong?
words.es: Flor, ¿me podés corregir si explico algo mal?
words.note: Informal Argentine vos: podés instead of puedes.

words.en: Is this your first time at the exchange?
words.es: ¿Es tu primera vez en el intercambio?

lessons.speaking: You are a regular at a Palermo language exchange, and the AI is Joaquín, a newcomer, with organizer Flor nearby: explain how the intercambio works and its unwritten rules using impersonal se and si + present (se habla…, si alguien no entiende, se pregunta).

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se habla media hora en español; si alguien no entiende, se pregunta)

examples.es: Se habla media hora en español y después se cambia al inglés.
examples.en: You speak Spanish for half an hour and then switch to English.

examples.es: Si alguien no entiende, se pregunta otra vez.
examples.en: If someone doesn't understand, you ask again.

lessons.title: Cook Your Family Recipe with a New Friend in Oaxaca
lessons.objective: Guide a friend through a recipe step by step and stop to check an ingredient label for an allergy.

words.note: Mexican word for a red tomato; tomate is used in most other countries.
Many Mexicans say el sartén; both are understood.
Labels say: puede contener trazas de... (may contain traces of...).
Mexico; in South America it's maní.

words.en: Chop the onion and pass it to me, please.
words.es: Pica la cebolla y pásamela, por favor.
words.note: Informal tú, fine with a friend.

words.en: Stir it slowly so it doesn't stick.
words.es: Revuélvelo despacio para que no se pegue.

words.en: Don't touch it yet; it's very hot.
words.es: No lo toques todavía; está muy caliente.

words.en: Wait, Beto, how serious is your allergy?
words.es: Espera, Beto, ¿qué tan grave es tu alergia?

words.en: Before we go on, let's read the package label.
words.es: Antes de seguir, leamos la etiqueta del paquete.

words.en: The label says: "May contain traces of nuts."
words.es: La etiqueta dice: "Puede contener trazas de nuez."

words.en: Better not to use it; we'll buy another one without nuts.
words.es: Mejor no lo usamos; compramos otro sin nueces.

words.en: Taste it and tell me if it needs salt.
words.es: Pruébalo y dime si le falta sal.

lessons.speaking: You are teaching the AI, your new friend Itzel, to cook your family recipe in a guesthouse kitchen in Oaxaca: guide each step with commands like córtalo, revuélvelo, no lo toques todavía and pásamelo, and check her work as you go.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (córtalo, revuélvelo, no lo toques todavía, pásamelo)

examples.es: Ponlo en la olla y revuélvelo despacio.
examples.en: Put it in the pot and stir it slowly.

examples.es: No lo abras todavía; primero léeme la etiqueta.
examples.en: Don't open it yet; first read me the label.

lessons.title: Read the Salsa School's Code of Conduct Together
lessons.objective: Read a dance social's code of conduct on consent and photos and explain it to another traveler.

words.note: For a woman: la instructora.

words.en: Before dancing, you have to ask the other person.
words.es: Antes de bailar, hay que preguntarle a la otra persona.

words.en: After a no, you have to accept it without insisting.
words.es: Después de un no, hay que aceptarlo sin insistir.

words.en: Greta, wait, let's read the code before going in.
words.es: Greta, espera, leamos el código antes de entrar.
words.note: Informal, between fellow travelers.

words.en: It says here you have to ask for permission before filming.
words.es: Aquí dice que hay que pedir autorización antes de grabar.

words.en: Wilson, what does this rule about filming other dancers mean?
words.es: Wilson, ¿qué significa esta norma sobre grabar a otros bailarines?

words.en: Could you explain what happens if someone films without permission?
words.es: ¿Me puede explicar qué pasa si alguien graba sin permiso?
words.note: Formal usted, for the instructor.

words.en: After dancing, you have to say thank you.
words.es: Después de bailar, hay que dar las gracias.

words.en: If you don't feel comfortable, you can say no.
words.es: Si no te sientes cómoda, puedes decir que no.
words.note: Informal tú to Greta; cómoda because she is a woman (cómodo for a man).

lessons.speaking: You are at a salsa school in Medellín, and the AI is Greta, a fellow traveler, with instructor Wilson nearby: read the posted code of conduct together, explain each rule with antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que, and ask Wilson (usted) about any unclear rule.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de bailar hay que preguntar; después de bailar se agradece)

examples.es: Antes de grabar, hay que pedirles permiso a todos.
examples.en: Before filming, you have to ask everyone for permission.

examples.es: Después de bailar, se agradece y se sale de la pista.
examples.en: After dancing, you say thank you and leave the floor.

lessons.title: The Restaurant Lost Your Dinner Date Reservation
lessons.objective: Explain to the host what happened with the booking and propose a solution, keeping your date at ease.

words.note: Peru and most of South America say reserva; reservación sounds Mexican.
Often shortened to la captura.
Peruvian word for small dishes to share at the table.
De cortesía means complimentary.

words.en: I made the reservation under my name for 8.
words.es: Hice la reserva a mi nombre para las 8.

words.en: When I called, they told me I didn't need to confirm.
words.es: Cuando llamé, me dijeron que no necesitaba confirmar.
words.note: Preterite for the call, imperfect for the background situation.

words.en: The young woman who was answering wrote down my last name and cell number.
words.es: La señorita que contestaba anotó mi apellido y mi celular.

words.en: Here is the screenshot of the confirmation email.
words.es: Aquí tiene la captura del correo de confirmación.
words.note: Formal: tiene for usted.

words.en: Could we wait at the bar until a table frees up?
words.es: ¿Podríamos esperar en la barra hasta que se libere una mesa?
words.note: Formal, polite proposal with the conditional.

words.en: Would there be a table available in the dining room later?
words.es: ¿Habría alguna mesa disponible en el salón más tarde?

words.en: Valeria, there was a problem with the reservation, but I'm sorting it out.
words.es: Valeria, hubo un problema con la reserva, pero ya lo arreglo.
words.note: Informal: tú with your date.

words.en: Do you feel like a pisco sour while we wait?
words.es: ¿Te provoca un pisco sour mientras esperamos?
words.note: Peruvian: ¿te provoca? means do you feel like it.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest, and the AI is Señor Paredes, the host at a Lima restaurant: explain how you booked with the preterite and imperfect (llamé, la persona que contestaba dijo...), propose solutions with the conditional (¿podríamos sentarnos en la barra?), and reassure Valeria.

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (llamé el martes, la persona que contestaba dijo...; ¿podríamos sentarnos en la barra?)

examples.es: Llamé el martes, y la persona que contestaba dijo que había mesa.
examples.en: I called on Tuesday, and the person who was answering said there was a table.

examples.es: ¿Sería posible cenar en la barra esta noche?
examples.en: Would it be possible to have dinner at the bar tonight?

lessons.title: Rain Cancels the Park Picnic: Pitch a Plan B
lessons.objective: Compare backup options with friends and agree on a new plan, time and meeting point for the afternoon.

words.note: Very common in Colombia for a heavy, sudden rain.
In Colombia sombrilla is the everyday word for umbrella.
Bogotá classic: you drop the cheese into the hot chocolate.
Colombian word; other countries say tráfico or atasco.
Agrees: empapada for a woman, empapados for a group.

words.en: According to the forecast, it's going to clear up after 3.
words.es: Según el pronóstico, va a escampar después de las 3.
words.note: Escampar means the rain stops.

words.en: With this downpour, the park is out.
words.es: Con este aguacero, el parque queda descartado.

words.en: The mall is going to be more crowded than the museum.
words.es: El centro comercial va a estar más lleno que el museo.

words.en: We'll get there faster on TransMilenio than by taxi in this traffic.
words.es: En TransMilenio llegaremos más rápido que en taxi con este trancón.

words.en: Sofía, the bookstore is quieter than the movie theater, don't you think?
words.es: Sofía, la librería es más tranquila que el cine, ¿no crees?
words.note: Informal: tú with a friend.

words.en: Andrés, I like your idea, but the movie theater is farther away.
words.es: Andrés, me gusta tu idea, pero el cine queda más lejos.

words.en: So we'll meet at 4 at the museum door.
words.es: Entonces nos vemos a las 4 en la puerta del museo.

words.en: Does that work for you, or should we vote?
words.note: Ustedes is the normal plural for friends in Colombia.

lessons.speaking: You are the friend who planned the picnic, and the AI plays Andrés and Sofía in Bogotá: compare the indoor options with más/menos ... que, predict with the future and ir a (va a escampar, llegaremos), and get the group to agree on one plan, time and meeting point.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (el museo va a estar más lleno que el café; lloverá menos por la tarde)

examples.es: Mañana hará más sol, pero hoy vamos a quedarnos bajo techo.
examples.en: Tomorrow will be sunnier, but today we're going to stay indoors.

examples.es: La chocolatería estará menos llena que el centro comercial.
examples.en: The chocolate shop will be less crowded than the mall.

lessons.title: Sort Out a Wrong Bar Tab with Five New Friends
lessons.objective: Reconstruct the round of orders with the manager and split the corrected bill fairly among the group.

words.note: Spain: a small glass of draft beer.

words.en: the red wine with lemon soda

words.note: Often just las bravas. Spain says patatas, not papas.
In Spain el ticket is the printed bill you check line by line.
Hacer un bote: everyone puts money into a shared pot.
Used as a verb phrase: te hago un Bizum.
Pagar a escote: everyone pays the same share.
Spain: camarero / camarera; mesero is Latin American.

words.en: We ordered 3 beers and 2 sharing plates, not 4.
Pablo paid for the first round at the bar.
words.es: Pablo pagó la primera ronda en la barra.

words.en: Rafa, here you charged us for 2 tintos de verano we didn't order.
words.es: Rafa, aquí nos cobraste 2 tintos de verano que no pedimos.
words.note: Tú with bar staff is normal in Madrid.

words.en: Can you go over the bill with us line by line?
words.es: ¿Nos puedes repasar el ticket línea por línea?

words.en: We sent the potatoes back, remember?
words.note: Ustedes (se acuerdan) for the group of friends.

words.en: Lucía, you only had water, so you pay less.
words.es: Lucía, tú solo tomaste agua, así que pagas menos.

words.en: Do we split it evenly or does everyone pay for their own?
words.es: ¿Lo pagamos a escote o cada uno lo suyo?

words.en: Pablo, I'll send you 12 euros by Bizum right now.
words.es: Pablo, ahora te hago un Bizum de 12 euros.

lessons.speaking: You are one of the six friends, and the AI is Rafa, the bar manager in La Latina: go through the ticket line by line, retell what the group ordered and who paid with the preterite (pedimos, Pablo pagó), keep the numbers straight, and split the corrected total fairly.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (pedimos tres cañas y dos raciones; Pablo pagó la primera ronda)

examples.es: Primero pedimos 6 cañas y luego Lucía pidió 1 media ración de croquetas.
examples.en: First we ordered 6 beers and then Lucía ordered 1 half portion of croquettes.

examples.es: Pablo pagó la primera ronda, así que esa no va en el ticket.
examples.en: Pablo paid for the first round, so that one doesn't go on the bill.

lessons.title: Refuse to Ride with a Friend Who Has Been Drinking
lessons.objective: Say no to getting in the car, discourage the driver firmly and arrange a safer ride home for the group.

words.note: Argentina: a car service you call by phone; plural los remises.
Argentina says ruta for a highway between towns.
Córdoba's signature drink, usually mixed with cola.
Polite way to say someone has been drinking: está tomado.
Agrees: sobria for a woman.
In Argentina stressed on the o: CHO-fer.
Argentina says auto; carro is not used there.

words.en: Nico, don't drive like this; you had a lot of fernet.
words.es: Nico, no manejes así; tomaste mucho fernet.

words.en: Ana, don't give him the keys, please.
words.es: Ana, no le des las llaves, por favor.

words.en: I don't recommend that anyone get in that car.
words.es: No recomiendo que nadie suba a ese auto.
words.note: No recomiendo que + subjunctive (suba).

words.en: I'm not getting in; I'd rather pay for a remís.
words.es: Yo no subo; prefiero pagar un remís.

words.en: Don't get mad; I'm saying it because I care about you.
words.es: No te enojes; lo digo porque me importás.
words.note: Argentine vos: importás, stress on the last syllable.

words.en: Can you give me the car service's number?
words.es: ¿Me pasás el número de la remisería?
words.note: Informal vos form: pasás.

words.en: Hi, we need a car for 4 people to the city of Córdoba.
words.es: Buenas, necesitamos un remís para 4 personas a Córdoba capital.
words.note: Neutral register for calling the dispatcher.

words.en: How much is the fare to downtown?
words.es: ¿Cuánto sale la tarifa hasta el centro?
words.note: Argentina: ¿cuánto sale? means how much does it cost.

lessons.speaking: You are a guest at the asado, and the AI plays Nico, who wants to drive everyone home, and Ana: refuse to ride, discourage Nico firmly but kindly with negative commands (no manejes, no le des las llaves) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, and arrange a remís.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no manejes, no le des las llaves; no recomiendo que nadie suba)

examples.es: No manejes esta noche; mañana buscás el auto.
examples.en: Don't drive tonight; you can pick up the car tomorrow.

examples.es: No recomiendo que nadie se suba hasta que llegue el remís.
examples.en: I don't recommend that anyone get in until the remís arrives.

lessons.title: Honest Feedback on a Friend's New Walking Tour
lessons.objective: Give a friend specific, kind feedback on his tour, naming strengths and two concrete changes to make.

words.note: Common in Mexico; you also hear "los comentarios".

words.en: What I liked most were your stories about the neighborhood.
words.es: Lo que más me gustó fueron tus anécdotas del barrio.

words.en: Diego, don't take it the wrong way; the tour is great.
words.es: Diego, no te lo tomes a mal; el tour está padrísimo.
words.note: Informal. "Padrísimo" is Mexican slang for really great.

words.en: I recommend you speak louder in the square.
words.es: Te recomiendo que hables más fuerte en la plaza.

words.en: I suggest you drop one stop so it's shorter.
words.es: Sugiero que quites una parada para que dure menos.

words.en: I'm not saying it's bad; I'm saying it feels long.
words.es: No digo que sea malo; digo que se siente largo.
words.note: "No digo que" takes the subjunctive: sea, not es.

words.en: I hope you add more fun facts at the end.
words.es: Ojalá que agregues más datos curiosos al cierre.

words.en: Do you want me to tell you what I really thought?
words.es: ¿Quieres que te diga lo que de verdad pensé?

lessons.speaking: You are a friend who joined Diego's trial walking tour, and the AI is Diego over coffee in Guadalajara: name two strengths and two concrete changes, kindly and honestly, using te recomiendo que, sugiero que and ojalá que with the subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (te recomiendo que hables más despacio; ojalá que incluyas el mercado)

examples.es: Te recomiendo que hables más despacio en la catedral.
examples.en: I recommend you speak more slowly at the cathedral.

examples.es: Ojalá que incluyas el mercado al final del recorrido.
examples.en: I hope you include the market at the end of the route.

lessons.title: Two Travel Friends Fall Out over a Comment
lessons.objective: Report what each friend said, separate facts from feelings and help them agree on how to move on.

words.note: Means an argument or quarrel, not a calm discussion.
A veiled remark aimed at someone: "lanzar una indirecta".
Use el compañero de cuarto for a man.
Andean word, used all the time in Cusco.
Feminine form for Marta or Lena; ofendido for a man.

words.en: Lena told me she felt ignored at breakfast.
words.es: Lena me dijo que se sentía ignorada en el desayuno.

words.en: Marta says she was just tired from the altitude sickness.
words.es: Marta dice que estaba cansada por el soroche, nada más.

words.en: Lena thought the comment was about her.
words.es: Lena pensaba que el comentario era sobre ella.

words.en: Let's separate what happened from what you felt.
words.es: Separemos lo que pasó de lo que sintieron.

words.en: What exactly did she say, word for word?
Neither of you wanted to offend the other.
words.es: Ninguna de las dos quería ofender a la otra.

words.en: How about we talk it over now, calmly?
words.es: ¿Les parece si lo hablamos ahora, con calma?
words.note: "Ustedes" for two people is normal in Latin America, formal or not.

words.en: So, do we agree you'll have breakfast together again tomorrow?
words.es: Entonces, ¿quedamos en que mañana desayunan juntas otra vez?

lessons.speaking: You are a fellow traveler in a Cusco hostel, and the AI plays Marta and then Lena: report what each one told you with dijo que and pensaba que plus the imperfect, separate facts from feelings, and help them agree on how to move on.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Marta dijo que estaba cansada; Lena pensaba que hablaba de ella)

examples.es: Marta dijo que estaba de mal humor por la altura.
examples.en: Marta said she was in a bad mood because of the altitude.

examples.es: Lena creía que Marta se reía de su acento.
examples.en: Lena believed Marta was laughing at her accent.

lessons.title: Keep the Group Going on a Long Volcano Hike
lessons.objective: Encourage a struggling friend, make clear commitments to the group and respect the guide's turnaround call.

words.note: The guide sets it; the group follows it.
Use la guía for a woman.
Guatemalan word for jacket.
Standard word of encouragement on a hard climb.

words.en: You're doing great, Rocío, keep going!
words.note: Informal, tú with a friend.

words.en: I'll carry your water until the next break.
words.es: Yo llevaré tu agua hasta el próximo descanso.

words.en: We'll get to camp together, step by step.
words.es: Llegaremos juntos al campamento, paso a paso.

words.en: Esteban, at exactly what time will we turn back?
If Esteban says we turn back, we'll turn back without arguing.
words.es: Si Esteban dice que regresamos, regresaremos sin discutir.

words.en: Rocío, if you feel dizzy, tell me and we'll tell Esteban.
words.es: Rocío, si te mareas, avísame y le decimos a Esteban.

words.en: Esteban, is it okay if Rocío walks up front, next to you?
words.es: Esteban, ¿le parece bien si Rocío camina adelante, junto a usted?
words.note: Formal: usted with the guide.

words.en: Breathe deeply; at the next break we'll eat something.
words.es: Respira hondo; en el próximo descanso comeremos algo.

lessons.speaking: You are hiking Acatenango with friends, and the AI is Rocío, who is tired, and then guide Esteban: encourage her with ¡ánimo! and vas muy bien, make commitments in the future tense (llevaré, llegaremos), and follow the guide's turnaround time.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (yo llevaré tu agua; llegaremos juntos; ¡vas muy bien, ánimo!)

examples.es: Yo cargaré tu mochila un rato.
examples.en: I'll carry your backpack for a while.

examples.es: ¡Lo lograremos juntos; vas muy bien!
examples.en: We'll make it together; you're doing great!

lessons.title: Your Teacher's Birthday Party: Usted and Tú
lessons.objective: Switch between usted and tú with each guest and make polite requests and offers at a home party.

words.note: Use el cumpleañero for a man.
Chile says torta; Mexico says pastel.
Chilean late-afternoon meal of bread, tea and snacks.
Fresh tomato, onion, cilantro and chili salsa.
Pino is the Chilean filling of beef, onion, egg and olive.
Standard in Chile.
Use la vecina for a woman.

words.en: Professor, would you mind if I take a photo of you with the cake?
words.es: Profesora, ¿le importaría si le tomo una foto con la torta?
words.note: Formal: usted.

words.en: I'd like to make a toast to Professor Inés.
words.es: Quisiera hacer un brindis por la profesora Inés.

words.en: Mateo, can you pass me the salsa?
words.note: Informal: tú with a teenager.

words.en: Don Hernán, can I pour you a bit more wine?
words.es: Don Hernán, ¿le sirvo un poco más de vino?
words.note: Formal: usted with an older neighbor.

words.en: Can I really call you tú, Professor?
words.note: Formal until she confirms; tutear means to address someone as tú.

words.en: So, Inés, can I help you with the dishes?
words.es: Entonces, Inés, ¿te ayudo con los platos?
words.note: Informal: tú after she asks for it.

words.en: Mateo, what grade are you in at school?
words.es: Mateo, ¿en qué curso estás en el colegio?
words.note: In Chile, curso means school grade.

words.en: It was a pleasure to meet you, Don Hernán.
words.es: Fue un gusto conocerlo, don Hernán.
words.note: Formal; use conocerla for a woman.

lessons.speaking: You are a guest at Profesora Inés Valdés's birthday in Santiago, and the AI plays Inés, her son Mateo and an older neighbor: greet each one, use usted or tú to fit each person, and make requests and offers with quisiera, ¿le importaría...? and ¿me pasas...?

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿le importaría...?, ¿me pasas...?)

examples.es: ¿Le importaría pasarme la servilleta, don Hernán?
examples.en: Would you mind passing me the napkin, Don Hernán?

examples.es: Mateo, ¿me pasas una empanada?
examples.en: Mateo, can you pass me an empanada?

lessons.title: Report a Stolen Phone at the Police Station
lessons.objective: Give police a clear timeline of the theft, describe the items and confirm the details on the written report.

words.note: In Spain you 'poner una denuncia' (file a report) at the comisaría.
Hurto is theft without violence; robo involves force or threats.
Spain says móvil; Latin America says celular.

words.en: I'm here to file a report for the theft of my phone.
words.es: Vengo a poner una denuncia por el hurto de mi móvil.
words.note: Formal, to the officer.

words.en: We got to the terrace at about eleven thirty.
words.es: Llegamos a la terraza a las once y media, más o menos.

words.en: I left the phone on the table, next to my glass.
words.es: Dejé el móvil encima de la mesa, al lado de mi copa.

words.en: About ten minutes later, I looked and it was gone.
words.es: Unos diez minutos más tarde, miré y ya no estaba.

words.en: It's a black phone with a blue case.
words.es: Es un móvil negro con una funda azul.

words.en: Excuse me, the time is wrong: we arrived at eleven thirty.
words.es: Perdone, la hora está mal: llegamos a las once y media.
words.note: Perdone is the polite usted form of 'excuse me'.

words.en: Before signing, can I read the statement again?
words.es: Antes de firmar, ¿puedo leer la declaración otra vez?

words.en: Can you give me a copy for my travel insurance?
words.es: ¿Me puede dar una copia para el seguro de viaje?

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is officer Jordi Puig: give a clear timeline of the theft with markers like a las once y media and unos diez minutos más tarde, describe the phone, and check every detail of the printed report before you sign it.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las once y media, después de salir del bar, unos diez minutos más tarde)

examples.es: A las once y media nos sentamos en la terraza.
examples.en: At eleven thirty we sat down on the terrace.

examples.es: Después de pagar, busqué el móvil y ya no estaba.
examples.en: After paying, I looked for my phone and it was gone.

lessons.title: Almost Got in an Unofficial Taxi: Talk It Through
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss with a friend without blame and agree on how you will get home next time.

words.note: Common Mexican term for an unlicensed cab.

words.en: the taxi from an official stand
words.note: In Mexico a sitio is a registered taxi stand.
Displayed inside licensed Mexico City taxis.
The hours after midnight, before sunrise.

words.en: Don't feel bad, Paola; it happens to anyone.
words.es: No te sientas mal, Paola; a cualquiera le pasa.
words.note: Informal, tú.

words.en: I almost got in too; it wasn't your fault.
words.es: Casi me subo yo también; no fue tu culpa.

words.en: We nearly got in, but in the end nothing happened.
words.es: Por poco subimos, pero al final no pasó nada.

words.en: It could have gone badly, but we reacted in time.
words.es: Podría haber salido mal, pero reaccionamos a tiempo.

words.en: What made you doubt the car at that moment?
words.es: ¿Qué te hizo dudar del coche en ese momento?

words.en: Before getting in, we compare the plate with the one in the app.
words.es: Antes de subir, comparamos la placa con la de la app.

words.en: If there's no signal, we look for a taxi from a stand.
words.es: Si no hay señal, buscamos un taxi de sitio.

words.en: I'll share my real-time location with you when we go out.
words.es: Te comparto mi ubicación en tiempo real cuando salgamos.
words.note: Informal, tú.

lessons.speaking: You are Paola's travel friend, and the AI is Paola: talk through last night's near miss calmly and without blame, using casi, por poco and podría haber salido mal, then agree on a plan for getting home with si clauses like si pasa otra vez, pedimos por la app.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco subimos; podría haber salido mal; si pasa otra vez, pedimos por la app)

examples.es: Por poco nos subimos a ese coche sin logotipo.
examples.en: We nearly got into that unmarked car.

examples.es: Si pasa otra vez, pedimos el coche por la app.
examples.en: If it happens again, we'll order the car through the app.

lessons.title: Call Emergency Services When a Friend Collapses
lessons.objective: Give the operator your location and the friend's condition, and follow and relay their instructions.

words.note: Agrees with the person: pálido for Jonas, pálida for a woman.

words.en: My friend has fainted; he's conscious but very pale.
words.es: Mi amigo se ha desmayado; está consciente pero muy pálido.
words.note: Spain often uses the present perfect for something that just happened.

words.en: We're by the main stage, next to the drinks stand.
words.es: Estamos junto al escenario principal, al lado del puesto de bebidas.

words.en: Yes, he's breathing, but he isn't responding well when I talk to him.
words.es: Sí, respira, pero no responde bien cuando le hablo.

words.en: Okay, I'll stay on the line.
words.es: Vale, me quedo en la línea.
words.note: Vale is the everyday Spain word for 'okay'.

words.en: If he gets worse, I'll let you know right away.
words.note: Formal, to the operator.

words.en: 112 says to put him in the shade, on his side.
words.es: El 112 dice que lo pongamos a la sombra, de lado.

words.en: Thanks, but we're following what 112 says.
words.es: Gracias, pero seguimos lo que dice el 112.
words.note: Polite but firm, for a bystander.

words.en: How long will the ambulance take to arrive?

lessons.speaking: You are at the festival with Jonas, and the AI is the 112 operator: give your exact location and Jonas's condition, use si + future like si no responde, le avisaré, and follow and relay commands such as quédese en la línea.

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short phone commands (si no responde, le avisaré; quédese en la línea; está en la plaza)

examples.es: Si no responde, le avisaré enseguida.
examples.en: If he doesn't respond, I'll let you know right away.

examples.es: Quédese en la línea; la ambulancia llegará pronto.
examples.en: Stay on the line; the ambulance will be there soon.

lessons.title: Police Respond to a Noise Complaint at Your Rental
lessons.objective: Answer an officer's questions formally, explain what steps were taken and confirm the quiet hours.

words.note: Set by each town's ordinance, so ask the officer instead of guessing.
Spain says piso for an apartment or flat.
Spain says altavoz; Latin America often says bocina.
Address her simply as agente.
Fixed apology: disculpe las molestias.

words.en: Good evening, officer. I'm sorry for the disturbance.
words.es: Buenas noches, agente. Disculpe las molestias.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: The music was turned down as soon as we were told.
words.es: Se bajó la música en cuanto nos avisaron.

words.en: The courtyard speaker was turned off at eleven.
words.es: Se apagó el altavoz del patio a las once.

words.en: The guests were told they had to keep their voices down.
words.es: Se avisó a los invitados de que había que bajar la voz.

words.en: The windows and the courtyard door were closed.
words.es: Se cerraron las ventanas y la puerta del patio.

words.en: Here are my ID papers and the rental agreement.
words.es: Aquí tiene mi documentación y el contrato de alquiler.
words.note: Formal: aquí tiene, for usted.

words.en: What quiet hours does the local ordinance set?
words.es: ¿Qué horario de descanso establece la ordenanza municipal?

words.en: Tomorrow we'll apologize to Mr. Ortega.
words.es: Mañana le pediremos disculpas al señor Ortega.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest renting the flat, and the AI is Agente Carmen Moreno: answer her questions formally with usted, explain what was done using passive se (se bajó la música, se avisó a los invitados), and ask her what quiet hours the ordinance sets.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se bajó la música, se avisó a los invitados, se cerraron las ventanas)

examples.es: Se pidió a los invitados que hablaran más bajo.
examples.en: The guests were asked to speak more quietly.

examples.es: Se cerraron las ventanas que dan al callejón.
examples.en: The windows facing the alley were closed.

lessons.title: Write to the Organizer About a Harassing Guest
lessons.objective: Write a factual, discreet email reporting a participant's behavior toward another guest at an event.

words.note: Keep it neutral, e.g. Asunto: incidente en el intercambio.
la participante for a woman.
el asistente for a man.
More formal than dirección; common in written reports.
la testigo for a woman.
tomar medidas = to take action.
Standard formal email closing, placed before your name.

words.en: I would like to inform you that there was a worrying incident last night.
words.es: Quisiera informarle de que anoche hubo un incidente preocupante.
words.note: Formal written register.

words.en: First of all, a participant repeatedly asked an attendee for her home address.
words.es: En primer lugar, un participante pidió repetidamente el domicilio de una asistente.

words.en: In addition, he kept insisting after she told him no.
words.es: Además, siguió insistiendo después de que ella le dijo que no.

words.en: Therefore, I ask you to take action before the next event.
words.es: Por lo tanto, le pido que tome medidas antes del próximo evento.
words.note: pedir que + subjunctive (tome).

words.en: To protect the attendee, I am not including her name or details.
words.es: Para proteger a la asistente, no incluyo su nombre ni sus datos.

words.en: She authorized me to write to you; she prefers her name not be shared.
words.es: Ella me autorizó a escribirle; prefiere que no se comparta su nombre.

words.en: Could you confirm what action you will take with this participant?
words.es: ¿Podría confirmarme qué medidas tomarán con este participante?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I look forward to your reply.
words.note: Write atenta if you are a woman.

lessons.speaking: You are an attendee of the language exchange, and the AI is organizer Paula Andrade, reading your email: report the facts in order with en primer lugar, además, por lo tanto and quisiera informarle de que, keeping Daniela's name and details out of it.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, además, por lo tanto, quisiera informarle de que...)

examples.es: Quisiera informarle de que un participante incomodó a una asistente.
examples.en: I would like to inform you that a participant made an attendee uncomfortable.

examples.es: Además, varias personas lo vieron; por lo tanto, hay testigos.
examples.en: In addition, several people saw it; therefore, there are witnesses.

lessons.title: Voice Notes: Your Bus Is Late for Tonight's Date
lessons.objective: Leave clear voice notes and texts to reschedule a date politely and confirm the new time and place.

words.note: Very common in Uruguay: mandame un audio.
Standard word for bus in Uruguay.
In Montevideo, the main one is Tres Cruces.
In Uruguay, a restaurant serving grilled meat.

words.en: Martina, sorry I'm late; the bus is running an hour behind.
words.es: Martina, perdoná el retraso; el ómnibus viene con una hora de demora.
words.note: Informal. Voseo command used in Uruguay; perdona elsewhere.

words.en: Would 9:30 work for you instead of 8?
words.es: ¿Te vendría bien a las 9:30 en vez de las 8?
words.note: Conditional vendría softens the request.

words.en: I'll let you know when I get to Tres Cruces.
words.es: Te aviso al llegar a Tres Cruces.

words.en: If your battery dies, we'll meet straight at the restaurant.
words.es: Si te quedás sin batería, nos vemos directo en la parrilla.
words.note: quedás is the vos form used in Uruguay.

words.en: Could you send me a quick voice message to confirm?
words.es: ¿Podrías mandarme un audio cortito para confirmar?

words.en: Don't worry about replying; an ok is enough for me.
words.es: No te preocupes por contestar; con un ok me alcanza.

words.en: Would you rather meet at the corner by the promenade?
words.es: ¿Te parecería mejor encontrarnos en la esquina de la rambla?

words.en: I called the restaurant and they'll hold our table until 10.
words.es: Llamé a la parrilla y nos guardan la mesa hasta las 10.

lessons.speaking: You are on a late bus to Montevideo, and the AI is Martina, your date: leave short voice notes to apologize, propose a new time and place, and confirm the plan, using ¿te vendría bien...?, perdoná el retraso and te aviso al llegar.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿te vendría bien a las nueve?, perdona el retraso, te aviso al llegar)

examples.es: ¿Te vendría bien cenar a las 9:30?
examples.en: Would 9:30 work for you for dinner?

examples.es: Perdoná la demora; te aviso al llegar a la terminal.
examples.en: Sorry for the delay; I'll let you know when I get to the terminal.

lessons.title: Your Partner Invites You Back: Discuss the Terms
lessons.objective: Talk honestly about returning to visit, setting conditions on time, money and expectations on both sides.

words.note: Costa Rica says tiquete; other countries say boleto or pasaje.
Takes the subjunctive when it sets a condition: siempre que pueda.

words.en: I would come back in March, as long as my boss gives me the time off.
words.es: Volvería en marzo, siempre que mi jefe me dé las vacaciones.
words.note: Costa Rica: usted is common even between partners.

words.en: I would stay a month if your family is okay with it.
words.es: Me quedaría un mes si a su familia le parece bien.

words.en: Doña Ruth, you're very kind, but I wouldn't want to be a burden.
words.es: Doña Ruth, es muy amable, pero no quisiera ser una carga.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Doña Ruth, would you allow me to contribute for the food?
words.es: Doña Ruth, ¿me permitiría aportar para la comida?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I would pay for my ticket, as long as I stay with you all.
words.es: Yo pagaría mi tiquete, siempre que me quede con ustedes.

words.en: Before saying yes, I'd like to talk about expectations.
words.es: Antes de decir que sí, quisiera hablar de expectativas.

words.en: I would only stay 2 weeks, unless I can work remotely.
words.es: Me quedaría solo 2 semanas, a menos que pueda teletrabajar.
words.note: a menos que always takes the subjunctive.

words.en: I'm not promising anything yet, but I really want to come back.
words.es: No le prometo nada todavía, pero de verdad quiero volver.
words.note: Affectionate usted, normal in Costa Rica.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler on your last evening in San José, and the AI is your partner Sebastián: talk honestly about coming back for a month and set clear terms on dates, money and expectations, using the conditional (volvería, me quedaría) and siempre que or a menos que + subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (volvería en marzo siempre que consiga vacaciones; me quedaría si a tu familia le parece bien)

examples.es: Volvería en marzo siempre que consiga vacaciones.
examples.en: I would come back in March as long as I get vacation time.

examples.es: Me quedaría un mes con tal de que me dejen ayudar con los gastos.
examples.en: I would stay a month provided that you let me help with the expenses.

lessons.title: Capstone: One Long Feria Day in Seville
lessons.objective: Lead a day out with new friends: explain plans, fix problems, handle an incident, send messages and say goodbye honestly.

words.note: What Sevillanos call the Feria grounds.
A classic meeting point.
Most casetas are private: you enter as a member's guest.

words.en: the sherry and lemon soda drink

words.note: Seville word for a dense crowd.
Formal police word for something lost, not stolen.
Spain's ID card; say de-ene-i.

words.en: Hugo, first we go to the entrance arch and then we go into the fairground.
words.es: Hugo, primero vamos a la portada y luego entramos al Real.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Here's the thing: the tent was private and the member can't invite us.
words.es: Les cuento: la caseta era privada y el socio no puede invitarnos.
words.note: Informal; les for a group of friends.

words.en: It's fine; look for a public tent while I ask around.
words.es: No pasa nada; busquen una caseta pública mientras yo pregunto.
words.note: Ustedes command to the group.

words.en: Officer, my friend has lost her wallet in the funfair area.
words.es: Agente, mi amiga ha perdido la cartera en la calle del Infierno.
words.note: Formal. Spain uses the perfect tense for something that just happened.

words.en: Where can she report the lost ID card?
words.es: ¿Dónde puede denunciar el extravío del DNI?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Álvaro, should we meet at 11 at the entrance arch instead?
words.es: Álvaro, ¿quedamos mejor a las 11 en la portada?
words.note: Informal. quedar = to arrange to meet, in Spain.

words.en: I'd love to come back next year, although I can't promise it.
words.es: Me encantaría volver el año que viene, aunque no puedo prometerlo.

words.en: If you ever go to the United States, it's on me.
words.es: Si algún día van a Estados Unidos, los invito yo.
words.note: Informal, ustedes.

lessons.speaking: You are leading a day at Seville's Feria, and the AI plays your friends and the people you meet: explain the plan to Hugo, handle whatever comes up using ustedes or usted as needed, text Álvaro, and say goodbye with honest plans using the conditional and subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar (connectors, commands, past narration, subjunctive, conditional, register switching)

examples.es: Mientras Irene buscaba su cartera, yo hablé con el agente.
examples.en: While Irene was looking for her wallet, I talked to the officer.

examples.es: Ojalá que nos veamos pronto, aunque no sé cuándo podré volver.
examples.en: I hope we see each other soon, although I don't know when I'll be able to come back.
